Two REPL bugs, both of them things that worked the last time you looked.

### A macro defined at the REPL was unbound on the next line

```
>>> (define-syntax swap! (syntax-rules () ((_ a b) (let ((t a)) (set! a b) (set! b t)))))
>>> (swap! p q)
Error: unbound variable swap!
```

The REPL evaluates one form at a time, and `Machine.Run` compiled each one.  A
compiled `define-syntax` expands its uses where it is compiled and defines
nothing, which is right inside a body and wrong for a sequence of top-level
forms: the macro never reached the environment.  `Run` now sends a form that
teaches the compiler something to the tree-walker — the same distinction
`CompileProgram` already made for whole files, so this covers macros, `import`
and `include`.

### Pasting a multi-line expression overwrote the prompt and the banner

The editor kept the pasted text in its buffer but stopped drawing it.  When
bracketed paste was made to insert at the cursor instead of at the end of the
line, the echo of the pasted bytes was dropped — and the redraw that follows
only rewrites what it knows about, so everything already on screen stayed where
it was and the pasted text landed on top of it:

```
GoScheme 3.1.2 (R7RS)
Type (exit) or press Ctrl->>> (+ 1
 2)
```

A paste is a change to the line like any other, so it now redraws the line the
same way every other edit does.

Verified in a real terminal (a pty), not by piping: one line, several lines, a
sixty-line block, two pastes in a row, a paste ending in a blank line, a paste
into the middle of a typed line, a paste onto a history entry, and typing the
first line of a definition by hand and pasting the rest.
